W2 (empirical), after E008. Best: E008, 6.977 s, 0.7572.

Measured (3 seeds, all complete):
E001 9ep eager 0.7430 / 9.43s. E002 10ep eager 0.7495 / 10.55s. E004 compiled+fused SGD 0.7486 / 9.04s. E005 +EMA 0.7583 / 9.10s. E006 +Muon 0.7649 / 9.45s. E007 +progressive res 0.7590 / 7.33s. E008 8.5ep 0.7572 / 6.98s.

Mechanisms:
1. Epoch dial: E007→E008 cost 0.5 epoch for -0.18 pp and -0.35 s (~4.8%). That is a shallower accuracy slope (~0.36 pp/epoch-half) than the eager pair (0.65 pp/epoch). Time per epoch is about 0.7 s. Margin over 0.753 is now 0.42 pp. Another 0.5 epoch cut would probably land near 0.7555 at ~6.6 s, with little safety left.
2. Compile: E003's slowness was a recompile leak, and E004 fixed it. Warmup must match the training shapes and strides.
3. EMA: +0.97 pp for +0.06 s. This is the cheapest gain measured.
4. Muon: +0.66 pp for +0.35 s.
5. Progressive resizing: -22% time for -0.59 pp. Time tracks pixel count. This is the biggest time lever per pp, and more aggressive schedules should still pay off, though returns diminish because fixed costs and small-kernel inefficiency grow as images shrink.
6. Noise: 3-seed accuracy ±0.2 pp. Time noise is unmeasured, probably 1-2%. Fixed costs (prepare, whitening, data upload, final EMA) are maybe 0.3-0.5 s, which are not reducible by epoch cuts.

Misses: I under-predicted EMA, Muon and resizing, because I was too skeptical. In E008 I was well calibrated. The epoch slope with EMA and Muon is shallower than I extrapolated from the eager pair.

Unsure: whether an LR floor of 0 adds anything on top of EMA; whether CUDA graphs help (the step is now short, so launch overhead matters under the 4-CPU pin); the 20 px floor; and the size of the fixed overhead.

forecasts.reason: Time is the 9 epoch E007 level (about 7.3 s, with noise). Accuracy gain from a LR floor of 0 is likely small but positive, since the final low-LR steps are partly redundant with EMA.
20 px start saves pixels, but accuracy probably drops ~0.5 pp from E007 (9 epochs), landing near the bar. Time falls to ~6.4 s.
Narrowing 576 to 512 cuts last-group FLOPs by ~20% but total only a few percent. This runs at 9 epochs, so time is around 7.0 s, with accuracy slightly lower than E007.
Diagnostic. Held-out seed mean should be within 0.3 pp of the seeds 0-2 mean, with per-seed std ~0.2-0.3 pp. A first epoch slower by ≥0.3 s is plausible.
CUDA graphs could save a few percent of launch overhead, but the risk of capture and compile problems is high. Accuracy matches E007 if it works. Time is relative to E007's 7.33 s.
BN stats recompute costs ~0.1 s. Lookahead resets already align the BN buffers, so the gain is likely under 0.3 pp.

cruxes: What is the fixed (epoch-independent) cost inside timed prepare+train? It sets how much further cutting epochs or resolution can save.
What is the true 40-seed mean accuracy of the E008 recipe? That is, is the 0.42 pp margin over 0.753 real, or is seed noise eating it?
Does a LR floor of 0 add accuracy on top of EMA? If it does, it buys about 0.5 epoch of cuts.
